methodHint.mwl: A general convention used in many countries. The standard here.

methodHint.dubai: A convention used in the Gulf.
methodHint.turkey: Turkey's Presidency of Religious Affairs, with its precaution minutes.
methodHint.singapore: The official bodies of Indonesia and Singapore.
methodHint.jafari: The usual Shia convention. Maghrib is a little after sunset, once the redness has left the sky.
methodHint.tehran: The University of Tehran, whose calendar Iran's official times follow.

disclaimer.short: SajdaTime is a helper, not a religious authority. These times are worked out on this computer from the position of the sun, using published calculation methods. They are not given by a mosque, a scholar, or any authority. I am not a Mufti, an Aalim, or an expert in fiqh, and this extension was built with the help of artificial intelligence. Software can carry faults, the computer can hold the wrong place or the wrong clock, and I can be wrong. Take what you see as a calculation, not a ruling. Where SajdaTime and your mosque disagree, follow your mosque. If something looks wrong or you are unsure, ask someone qualified. SajdaTime is free and given as it is, with no warranty and no promise of accuracy. And one request, if you would: please remember me, my family, and my parents in your duas.
disclaimer.full.1: SajdaTime is a helper, not a religious authority.
disclaimer.full.2: These times are not given to me by a mosque, a scholar, or any authority. Your computer works them out from the position of the sun, using calculation methods that Islamic authorities and scholars have published. I am not a Mufti, Aalim, or an expert in fiqh, and this extension was built with the help of artificial intelligence. Software can carry faults, a computer can hold the wrong location or the wrong clock, a closed browser or a sleeping computer can delay an alert, and I can simply be wrong.
disclaimer.full.3: So please take what you see here as a calculation and not a ruling. Where SajdaTime and your mosque disagree, follow your mosque. If a time looks off to you, or you are unsure, ask them or someone else qualified to advise you. The extension is free and is given as it is, with no warranty and no promise of accuracy, so where being exact matters to you, please do not rely on it alone.
disclaimer.full.4: Mosques do not all agree on when a prayer starts. Isha varies the most. In Britain and further north the gap between one method and another can be over an hour, because scholars measure the fading of the twilight differently. I cannot settle that, and the extension does not try to. If the times here do not match your mosque, ask them which method they use and pick it in Settings, under Calculation method. Where a difference remains, follow your mosque.
disclaimer.full.5: One more thing. This extension shows when a prayer becomes due. Your mosque then sets its own time for the congregation, usually a little later, so the board there and the times here will often differ. Neither is wrong.
disclaimer.full.6: And one request, if you would: please remember me, my family, and my parents in your duas.
